Audit logs: retention, retention location and exports
Data residency and private deployment options
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-29 15:00 EDT | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Alex Turner (Redwood AE), Samira Gupta (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neal (Redwood), J. Martinez (Crestwood Head of Security), Priya Rao (Vendor Risk), Ethan Cole (Cloud Architect)

Summary (auto): Quick SIG walkthrough, clarify evidence expectations, confirm scope of SOC 2, discuss keys/KMS and data residency options. Next: exchange documents and schedule evidence handoff.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Quick round-robin? We'll run the SIG spreadsheet together and call out evidence items.
[00:12] J. Martinez: Yep, thanks Alex. Priya, Ethan, I'm on the line. We're the vendor risk team looking to validate controls for a mid-tier fund product - some PII, some financial metadata. Looking for a clear path to evidence on your side.
[00:26] Priya: Hi all, also interested in data residency, whether data leaves the EU, and details on key management.
[00:33] Samira (SE): Great. We'll start high level — SOC 2 scope, then RBAC/SSO, then the SIG rows that usually cause questions, then evidence handoff. Any must-ask constraints before we begin?
[00:44] Ethan: Timeline is roughly two weeks for initial vendor assessment. We need high-priority items answered first - encryption, access controls, logging.
[00:52] Alex: Understood. Quick housekeeping: some of our docs are redacted versions of SOC 2 Type II, and we can provide a network diagram and KMS architecture sketch. I will upload links after this call.
[01:02] Priya: When you say KMS architecture, do you have customer-managed keys or only provider-managed? That's key for us.
[01:09] Samira: Good question. For hosted Redwood API we offer provider-managed KMS by default (encryption at rest with per-tenant keys); for Dedicated or Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS or HSM integration. In short: both models are possible depending on deployment.
[01:29] J. Martinez: Ok, and policies? We need key rotation, separation of duties, roles - proof.
[01:36] Samira: We have rotation policies and key lifecycle docs. We can provide a snippet of our KMS policy and an architecture sketch showing where keys live and which services have access. We'll mark which components are allowed to call the KMS — that's often asked in SIG evidence.
[01:53] Speaker 4: (muffled) can you share retention numbers for logs?
[01:56] Alex: Sure — standard hosted plan has 90 days of detailed request logs by default, retention options are configurable for Dedicated/Private. We also export immutable audit logs for enterprise packages.
[02:09] Ethan: Do you support sending logs to our SIEM? We prefer push to S3 or syslog to our Splunk.
[02:16] Samira: Yes. We support export of audit logs to customer-owned S3 buckets or streaming to a partner SIEM via secure transfer. There are RBAC constraints on who can enable exports. We'll include the docs that explain the setup steps.
[02:29] J. Martinez: On SOC 2, is the scope limited to the control plane or does it include data plane processing?
[02:37] Alex: Our SOC 2 typically covers the Redwood control plane and the hosted inference service. For Private deployments we provide SOC artifacts but customers often run their own compliance for the on-prem parts — we document the shared responsibilities. We'll clarify in the evidence packet which components are tested.
[02:54] Priya: Do you have ISO 27001 as well?
[02:58] Samira: Not yet ISO, but we have an ISO roadmap and parts of our security program align to ISO controls. SOC 2 Type II is our current formal report.
[03:08] Priya: ok.
[03:10] Alex: Let's jump into the SIG. Priya, Ethan — did you prefill any rows or do you want us to walk from top?
[03:18] Priya: We uploaded a partially completed SIG and flagged about 20 rows as high priority. We'll share a link in chat. The main areas: encryption, IAM, third-party management, incident response.
[03:27] Samira: Perfect. We'll go row-by-row for the flagged items.

[03:45] [SIG row: Encryption - at rest/transit]
[03:47] Samira: For encryption at rest we use AES-256, and in transit TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers. For hosted customers keys are rotated per our policy. For Dedicated you can bring your own keys via cloud KMS or an HSM. Evidence: we can provide crypto config docs, KMS architecture diagram, and rotation policy excerpt.
[04:12] Ethan: Do you support envelope encryption and customer-supplied wrapping keys?
[04:17] Samira: Yes, envelope encryption with customer-supplied keys is supported in Private and Dedicated flows. There's a short setup and an approval checklist for BYOK. We'll include the checklist.
[04:26] J. Martinez: Any independent attestation of the key management procedures?
[04:30] Alex: Our SOC 2 covers certain key management controls; we can point to the control IDs and the tests performed. For HSM attestation we can provide vendor certificates where applicable.

[05:00] [SIG row: RBAC / SSO / Provisioning]
[05:02] Samira: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle. RBAC is role-based within the console; API keys are scoped to projects and can be rotated. Evidence: SSO metadata, role matrix, audit log samples showing provisioning events.
[05:23] Priya: SCIM is a must for us. Any lag or eventual consistency caveats?
[05:28] Samira: SCIM is near real-time; typical syncs within seconds to a couple minutes depending on customer side. We'll include a short note about eventual consistency and token refresh behavior.

[05:50] [07:00] Alex: Quick aside — sometimes our transcriber turns KV cache into K V cash in the notes, so apologies if that shows up.
[07:06] J. Martinez: (laughs) noted.

[07:20] [SIG row: Audit logs and retention]
[07:22] Samira: Audit logs capture admin actions, API calls, and model invocation metadata. Default retention 90 days; long-term retention and egress to customer S3 or SIEM are supported. Evidence: sample audit log record (redacted), retention policy, and export playbook.
[07:42] Ethan: We need proof the logs include request IDs and the user/principal.
[07:47] Samira: Yes, logs include request ID, principal identity, action, timestamp, and resource. We will include a sample (redacted).

[08:05] [08:30] Priya: For the SIG CAIQ mapping, how granular is your evidence mapping? Do you map a single SOC control to multiple SIG rows?
[08:38] Samira: We usually map SOC controls to SIG/CAIQ rows with a matrix. Some SOC control IDs will map to multiple SIG questions; we'll share a mapping spreadsheet with the upload.

[09:00] [09:40] J. Martinez: On data residency — can you guarantee data stays in our EU region?
[09:45] Alex: Yes, we have regional hosting. For hosted customers you can pick a region and we ensure inference and logs remain in that region; for extra assurance, Dedicated/Private deployments keep everything in your VPC. Evidence: Region deployment diagram and data flow.
[09:59] Ethan: Do you do cross-region replication for disaster recovery that would move data?
[10:04] Samira: For hosted we may replicate metadata for DR within the region group; we can add a configuration that prevents replication outside a region — we'll detail the DR options.

[10:30] [11:00] Priya: Incident response — what's your notification SLA for a confirmed breach?
[11:06] Alex: For enterprise customers we offer breach notification timelines per contract; default is 72 hours for confirmed incidents with escalation channels. We'll include our incident response runbook excerpt and a redacted incident timeline example.
[11:21] J. Martinez: Do you have tabletop exercise evidence?
[11:25] Samira: We run regular exercises; can provide an after-action summary for a recent drill.

[11:45] [12:00] Ethan: Can we talk about model outputs for a second — do you retain model outputs and are they considered customer data?
[12:09] Samira: Model outputs from one customer's request are isolated; by default we do not use customer prompts/outputs for training. We can provide policy and an architecture note showing separation. Some older models had telemetry flags but we have customer-config flags to opt out. Evidence: Data retention policy and config flags screenshot.

[12:40] [13:00] Alex: Ok moving to third-party management — we keep a vendor inventory, attestations, and evidence for critical vendors. For SIG rows requiring vendor contracts, we'll provide redacted contracts and vendor SOC reports where available.
[13:15] Priya: Can you share your top third-party list? We need the subprocessor list for our procurement.
[13:20] Alex: We'll include a redacted subprocessor list.

[14:00] [14:30] J. Martinez: A few SIG rows ask for sample configuration screenshots from the console for RBAC and policy settings. Is that possible?
[14:36] Samira: Yes — screenshots of the role matrix and a sample audit log view can be provided, redacted for PII. We'll include step-by-step for granting cross-team access.

[15:00] [15:20] Priya: Evidence chain is important. If you provide a sample, we need to know where it came from and how current it is.
[15:27] Alex: Understood — we'll timestamp all evidence and include a short metadata sheet per artifact: source, timestamp, redaction notes.

[15:45] [16:00] Ethan: For Dedicated, can we put the entire service in our VPC and have all egress blocked?
[16:06] Samira: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC-only endpoints and private networking. Private deployments (on prem) are also an option for fully air-gapped requirements. We'll detail networking diagrams and firewall/IP allow lists in the upload.

[16:40] [17:00] J. Martinez: Regarding audits, do you support SOC 2 Type II observation for a customer in-scope? Like can an auditor come and view?
[17:07] Alex: We can support auditor access for hosted components subject to NDA and scheduling. For Private deployments auditors would review the customer's on-prem parts. We'll outline auditor access process in the docs.

[17:40] [18:00] Priya: A lot of our questions are procedural — change management, patching cadence.
[18:05] Samira: Our change mgmt policy includes emergency and scheduled windows, patching cadence and vulnerability management program; we'll include the vulnerability mgmt summary and policy excerpt.

[19:00] [19:30] Alex: Quick pause — anyone have red flags so far?
[19:33] Priya: Nothing blocking. Mostly need the artifacts.
[19:36] Ethan: Agree.

[19:50] [21:00] Samira: We'll also call out which SIG rows we can't answer because they're out of scope (e.g., questions about customer-managed on-prem network appliances if you run on-prem). We'll add clarifying notes to the mapping.

[21:30] [22:00] J. Martinez: For the evidence handoff — do you prefer to share via secure link or upload to our secure portal?
[22:06] Alex: We typically upload to a secure S3 link and can also push to a customer portal if you provide secure upload endpoints. We'll follow Crestwood's portal if you prefer.

[22:30] [23:00] Priya: Who will be the single point of contact for evidence questions?
[23:05] Alex: I'll be the primary contact — Alex Turner, and Samira will be technical lead for any follow-ups.

[23:20] [24:00] Samira: Practical note on evidence: some items will be redacted (usernames, IPs). We'll clearly label what's redacted and provide an unredacted view under NDA if needed for auditors.

[24:20] [25:00] Ethan: Regarding audit logs schema — are they JSON lines with consistent schema?
[25:06] Samira: Yes, they are JSONL with documented schema. We'll include the schema and sample.

[26:00] [27:00] J. Martinez: A couple of SIG rows ask about crypto algorithm settings — can you provide ciphersuites and parameter sizes?
[27:08] Samira: Sure — TLS 1.2/1.3 with recommended ciphers, RSA/ECDSA keys sizes per our crypto policy. We'll include crypto config docs.

[28:00] [29:00] Priya: For retention, if we ask for 7 years for some logs — possible?
[29:05] Alex: Long retention is possible by exporting to your S3. Storage costs and egress will be detailed in the pricing note.

[30:00] [31:00] Samira: On the topic of model telemetry — we will supply a policy that states we do not use customer prompts/outputs for model training without explicit opt-in. We'll include the policy screenshot.

[31:30] [32:00] Ethan: Network segmentation — can the inference runtime be restricted to a particular subnet?
[32:06] Samira: For Dedicated/Private yes. For hosted, we isolate per-tenant but not at customer-controlled subnet level unless Dedicated. We'll add notes.

[33:00] [34:00] Priya: A small question on SSO: do you support multiple SAML providers?
[34:07] Alex: Yes, multi-IDP is supported; SCIM mapping per IDP is configurable.

[34:30] [35:00] J. Martinez: Can you show an example of an access review artifact?
[35:06] Samira: We'll provide an access review template and a recent redacted example.

[35:40] [36:00] Priya: Any outstanding legal concerns? Contracts team will review Data Processing Agreement and Standard Contract Clauses for EU.
[36:09] Alex: We have DPA and SCC templates; will attach.

[36:40] [37:00] Ethan: Do you support customer-supplied HSMs?
[37:05] Samira: Yes, in Private deployments you can bring an HSM or integrate a cloud HSM for BYOK. We'll lay out the integration steps.

[37:40] [38:00] Alex: Ok, to keep this pragmatic — we'll upload a package with: redacted SOC 2 Type II, KMS architecture sketch, network diagram, audit log sample, role matrix screenshot, and mapping spreadsheet that shows which SOC controls map to which SIG rows.

[38:30] Priya: Great. Can you include timestamps on those artifacts?
[38:34] Alex: Yes.

[38:50] [40:00] Speaker 4: (inaudible) question about retention location
[40:02] Samira: Retention location mirrors region selection for hosted; exports can be to customer region buckets. We'll document constraints.

[40:30] [42:00] J. Martinez: Any final caveats about evidence we should know?
[42:05] Alex: Some evidence references third-party docs that may be gated — we'll note where a vendor cert is required and provide redaction notes. Also, some operational artifacts are time-bounded — we'll include recency metadata.

[42:30] [44:00] Priya: Sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
[44:05] Alex: Recap: Alex to upload evidence bundle by 2025-10-01; Samira to upload technical artifacts (KMS sketch, network diagram) by 2025-10-03; Crestwood to finalize SIG spreadsheet and flag any extra rows by 2025-10-06; schedule 30-min evidence handoff week of 2025-10-06.
[44:30] Priya: Confirmed. We'll also share our portal link for secure uploads.
[44:36] Ethan: We'll add legal review sprint after evidence handoff.

[45:00] [46:00] J. Martinez: Thanks everyone. One last ask — can you confirm whether logs include model input hashes so we can verify provenance without sending raw prompts?
[46:10] Samira: Yes we can include content hashes as part of the log record so you can verify provenance. We'll include the schema field name and an example.

[46:30] Alex: Great. If nothing else, we'll close. Thanks for the practical discussion.
[46:36] Priya: Thanks.
[46:38] Ethan: Thanks, bye.
[46:40] Alex: Bye all.

Post-call notes: Evidence upload links to be shared in CRM comment thread. Action owners noted.

(transcription notes: occasional mis-ATTribution and minor auto-transcript errors present; some technical terms spelled phonetically.)
